name: Morva Deep Cocoa Bar
description: A 30g bar of authenticated 68% real cacao chocolate, sourced from a controlled vertical farm operation and certified by the Meridian Food Authenticity Board. Comes in a sealed matte-black box with a holographic provenance tag.
flavor_profile: True dark chocolate — complex fruit and tobacco notes, genuine bitterness, long finish with a faint acidity; nothing synthetic approximates this and both eater and brand know it
cultural_context: Morva bars are gifted at major life events — promotions, births, deals closed. Eating one alone is considered either deeply self-indulgent or deeply sad depending on context. The holographic provenance tag is frequently scanned at social gatherings as a status display.
story_hooks: A batch of Morva bars is circulating with fraudulent provenance tags — the chocolate inside is high-quality synth-analog, nearly indistinguishable, but the scandal would be enormous if verified.
A Tier 1 character comes into possession of a Morva bar through unclear means and must decide whether to eat it, sell it, or use it as a social tool — each choice has significant consequences.

Morva's vertical farm operation sits on land that a Shelf expansion project would need — the corponation that wants the land is offering Morva a relocation deal that would compromise their supply chain and, quietly, their flavor profile.
